heading: INT. RED CANYON TRADING POST - AFTERNOON

units.text: INT. RED CANYON TRADING POST - AFTERNOON
A long adobe room with a plank counter and shelves of flour, tobacco, and tin cups.
Shafts of afternoon light cross the dust.
A stuffed buffalo head looks down from the back wall, one glass eye missing.
A stove burns low.
Behind the counter stands EZEKIEL TALLCHIEF-ROURKE, sixty, the proprietor, gray-bearded, with sleeves rolled to the elbow.
At a corner table sit two cowhands, WILEY BARNES, thirties, long and sunburned, playing solitaire, and JOSIAH COLTRANE, twenties, round-faced and quiet, whittling.
A fourth man, REV. ABEL MOREHOUSE, fifties, sits by the window in a dusty black coat, reading from a small Bible without looking at the words.
A clock ticks.
The whittling stops.
Coffee's on if you want it.
units.name: EZEKIEL

units.text: I'd take a cup.
units.name: WILEY

units.text: Josiah?
units.name: EZEKIEL

units.text: No, thank you, sir.
units.name: JOSIAH

units.text: Reverend?
units.name: EZEKIEL

units.text: I'm well, Mr. Rourke.
units.name: REV. MOREHOUSE

units.text: Ezekiel pours Wiley a cup and sets it on the table.
Wiley turns a card, grunts.
Hot enough to scald a snake.
units.name: WILEY

units.text: That's how you know it's coffee.
units.name: EZEKIEL

units.text: My ma used to say a man who drinks cold coffee has nothing to hurry for.
units.name: JOSIAH

units.text: Your ma sounds like a sensible woman.
units.name: EZEKIEL

units.text: She was, sir.
units.name: JOSIAH

units.text: Wiley glances at Josiah, then at the reverend, then down at his cards.
He lays down another.
The clock ticks louder.
Reverend, you've been on that same page for twenty minutes.
units.name: WILEY

units.text: It's a long verse.
units.name: REV. MOREHOUSE

units.text: It's one line.
units.name: WILEY

units.text: Then it has a lot to say.
units.name: REV. MOREHOUSE

units.text: Ezekiel wipes the counter with a gray rag, slow, circular.
Outside, a horse nickers.
He looks toward the window and then back at his rag.
Wiley, I don't believe I've asked where you're headed.
units.name: EZEKIEL

units.text: South.
units.name: WILEY

units.text: South's a big direction.
units.name: EZEKIEL

units.text: It's the only one I've got.
units.name: WILEY

units.text: We're delivering cattle to Dalton.
units.name: JOSIAH

units.text: Josiah.
units.name: WILEY

units.text: Sorry, Wiley.
units.name: JOSIAH

units.text: Silence.
The reverend turns a page.
The stove ticks.
Dalton's a fine town. I knew a man there once. Tall fella. Scar on his lip. Went by Cutter.
units.name: EZEKIEL

units.text: Wiley does not move.
Josiah's knife hangs in the air over the wood.
Funny thing. He used to come in here and play solitaire. Same as you. Always laid the black eight on the red nine.
units.name: EZEKIEL

units.text: Wiley looks down at the table.
The black eight lies on the red nine.
Coincidence.
units.name: WILEY

units.text: That's what I told myself.
units.name: EZEKIEL

units.text: The reverend closes his Bible.
He slips a hand inside his coat.
Josiah drops the knife and rises, hands wide.
Ezekiel does not stop wiping the counter.
He bends, as if reaching for a bottle, and comes up with a double-barreled shotgun pointed at the table.
Gentlemen. There's a marshal in the next room. He's been listening.
units.name: EZEKIEL

units.text: Mr. Rourke. I am the marshal.
units.name: REV. MOREHOUSE

units.text: He opens his coat to reveal a star pinned to the lining.
Wiley slowly lays down his cards.
Well, I'll be.
units.name: WILEY

units.text: You may be, son. The trial's in Dalton.
units.name: EZEKIEL
